projectContext.description: voiceover-matcher-subtitle: AI-powered pipeline for matching voiceover to stock footage

userStories.title: Generate sprint stories for caption focus area
acceptanceCriteria: Read scripts/ralph/config/ralph-config.json to understand the 'caption' focus area
Read scripts/ralph/session/prompt.md for project context and architecture notes
Read scripts/ralph/state/queue.json for interview details (story outline, architecture decisions, key files)
Read CLAUDE.md for project conventions and known issues
Analyze the codebase to find 8-12 specific improvements for 'caption'
Add stories US-73-002 through US-73-012 to scripts/ralph/state/prd.json (MUST use sprint-prefixed IDs)
Each story MUST have 4-6 testable acceptance criteria
Each story MUST have a 'notes' field with: (1) tier classification, (2) exact source file paths, (3) line number ranges if removing/moving code
IMPORTANT: All generated stories MUST have passes set to false - do NOT run tests or evaluate whether they already pass
IMPORTANT: Story IDs MUST follow format US-73-NNN to be unique across sprints
Mark this story (US-73-001) as passes: true when done
userStories.notes: Seed story - generated 11 stories (US-73-002 through US-73-012) covering caption system improvements: video-side chapter mapping, description relevance scoring, chapter-enriched embeddings, caption cache backward compatibility, caption quality tiered penalties, caption segment deduplication, caption fetcher retry logging, description-derived LLM reranker context, tag propagation to iterative match, caption timing gap detection, and chapter metadata in OTIO output.

userStories.title: Map video caption segments to video chapters during caption fetch
acceptanceCriteria: In caption_stage.py _populate_text_metadata(), after propagating video_chapters to VideoSearchResult, also map each caption segment to its containing video chapter using timestamp overlap
Each text_metadata entry gains 'chapter_index' and 'chapter_title' fields populated from the video's chapter list
Segments spanning chapter boundaries are assigned to the chapter with greatest temporal overlap
Segments outside all chapter boundaries get chapter_index=-1 and chapter_title=''
Unit test verifies chapter mapping with 3+ chapters and segments at boundaries, midpoints, and outside ranges
userStories.notes: HARD STORY: Skipped after 3_failures - pending decomposition

userStories.title: Add description-based relevance scoring adjustment
acceptanceCriteria: New method apply_description_relevance() in src/matching/scoring.py extracts keywords from video description and compares to voiceover segment text
Graduated boost: 1 keyword match +0.02, 2+ matches +0.04, 3+ matches +0.06, added to confidence_breakdown as 'description_relevance'
apply_all_adjustments() calls apply_description_relevance() with video_description parameter
Description is truncated to first 200 chars before keyword extraction to avoid noise from long descriptions
Unit test verifies graduated boost values and confidence_breakdown entry for 0, 1, 2, and 3+ keyword matches
userStories.notes: Implemented apply_description_relevance() with graduated boosts (+0.02/+0.04/+0.06), 200-char truncation, wired into apply_all_adjustments. 9 unit tests pass.

userStories.title: Add chapter-enriched embedding text for video segments
acceptanceCriteria: In caption_stage.py _populate_text_metadata(), when title_enriched_embeddings is enabled AND the segment has a mapped chapter, format embedding_text as '[{video_title} | {chapter_title}] {segment_text}'
When segment has no chapter (chapter_index=-1), fall back to existing '[{video_title}] {segment_text}' format
New config field context_enrichment.chapter_enriched_embeddings (bool, default true) controls this behavior
Config field added to both ContextEnrichmentConfig dataclass and config.yaml with inline comment
Unit test verifies embedding_text format with and without chapter, and with config toggle off
userStories.notes: Added chapter_enriched_embeddings config field (default true) to ContextEnrichmentConfig and config.yaml. Modified _populate_text_metadata to format embedding_text as '[Title | Chapter] text' when segment has chapter, falling back to '[Title] text'. 4 new tests in test_title_enriched_embeddings.py covering chapter enrichment on/off and mixed scenarios.

userStories.title: Add backward-compatible cache deserialization for CaptionResult metadata fields
acceptanceCriteria: CaptionResult.from_dict() (or equivalent deserialization) gracefully handles missing video_description, video_chapters, and video_tags keys by defaulting to '' and [] respectively
Existing cached caption results without these fields load without errors or warnings
Round-trip test: serialize CaptionResult with metadata, deserialize, verify all fields preserved
Round-trip test: serialize CaptionResult WITHOUT metadata fields (simulating old cache), deserialize, verify defaults applied
Unit test covers both dict-based and JSON-string-based cache formats
userStories.notes: All 5 criteria verified. CachedCaption.from_dict() is the equivalent deserialization path for CaptionResult. 16 tests cover: missing metadata defaults to empty, no warnings on old cache load, full round-trip with/without metadata, and both dict-based and JSON-string-based formats.

userStories.title: Add tiered caption quality penalties to scoring based on quality level
acceptanceCriteria: apply_caption_quality_adjustment() in scoring.py uses graduated penalties: auto_generated=-0.05, low_quality=-0.08, missing_timing=-0.03 (currently may use flat values)
Each penalty type appears as a separate entry in confidence_breakdown (e.g., 'caption_quality_auto', 'caption_quality_low', 'caption_timing_gap')
When multiple quality issues exist on a single segment, penalties stack (up to configurable max_caption_penalty, default -0.12)
Config fields for each penalty value added to MatchingConfig with defaults matching the values above
Unit test verifies each penalty individually and stacking behavior with cap
userStories.notes: Added apply_tiered_caption_penalties() with graduated penalties: auto_generated=-0.05, low_quality=-0.08, missing_timing=-0.03. Penalties stack up to configurable max_caption_penalty (-0.12). Each appears as separate breakdown entry (caption_quality_auto, caption_quality_low, caption_timing_gap). Config fields added to MatchingConfig. 11 tests all pass.

userStories.title: Detect and deduplicate overlapping caption segments
acceptanceCriteria: New function deduplicate_caption_segments() in src/caption/models.py takes a list of CaptionSegment and returns deduplicated list
Segments with >80% temporal overlap AND >70% text similarity (normalized Levenshtein or token overlap) are merged, keeping the one with higher text quality (longer text, fewer repeated chars)
Merged segments log the deduplication at DEBUG level with segment indices
CaptionResult gains a post-processing step that calls deduplication after segment parsing
Unit test with overlapping segments verifies merge behavior, and non-overlapping segments pass through unchanged
userStories.notes: Tier: Data quality. Files: src/caption/models.py (CaptionResult, CaptionSegment). Some YouTube captions (especially auto-generated) produce overlapping segments with near-identical text, inflating segment count and creating duplicate matches downstream. Deduplication at the caption level prevents this from propagating.

userStories.title: Add structured retry logging to caption fetcher for budget diagnostics
acceptanceCriteria: Each caption fetch attempt logs a structured dict with keys: video_id, attempt_number, success (bool), error_type (str or None), duration_ms, method ('captions', 'transcription')
At end of caption stage, a summary log entry shows: total_attempts, success_count, failure_count, error_type_distribution (dict of error_type to count), avg_duration_ms
Summary is also written to checkpoint under 'caption_stage_metrics' key for post-run analysis
Existing CaptionRetryBudget logging is preserved; new logging supplements (does not replace) it
Unit test verifies structured log entries are produced for success and failure cases
userStories.notes: Tier: Diagnostics. Files: src/caption_fetcher.py (fetch methods), src/stages/caption_stage.py (stage execution), src/caption/retry_budget.py. Currently retry budget tracks aggregate stats but individual attempt outcomes aren't structured-logged for post-hoc analysis. When caption budgets exhaust, diagnosing WHY requires manual log parsing.

userStories.title: Inject video tags into iterative match gap-filling search queries
acceptanceCriteria: In gap_analyzer.py, when generating search queries for a gap, check if the matched video sources near the gap have video_tags available
Extract up to 3 most relevant tags (by frequency across nearby matched segments) and append as query refinement terms
New config field iterative_match.use_tag_queries (bool, default true) controls this behavior
Tags containing generic terms ('video', 'youtube', 'official') are filtered out via a stop-tag list
Unit test verifies tag extraction from nearby matches and stop-tag filtering
userStories.notes: Tier: Quality improvement. Files: src/iterative_match/gap_analyzer.py (search query generation ~line 909+), src/config/sections/iterative_matching.py. Video tags from matched videos provide domain-specific vocabulary that can improve gap-filling queries. E.g., if matched videos have tags ['marine biology', 'coral reef'], gap queries should include those terms.

userStories.title: Detect and report caption timing gaps and coverage holes
acceptanceCriteria: New function analyze_caption_coverage() in src/caption/models.py computes: total_video_duration, total_captioned_duration, coverage_ratio, gap_count, largest_gap_seconds
Gaps are periods >2 seconds between consecutive segment end_time and next start_time where no caption text exists
CaptionResult gains a 'coverage_analysis' property that returns this analysis (computed lazily and cached)
When coverage_ratio < 0.7, a WARNING log is emitted with the video_id and gap details
Unit test verifies coverage computation with full coverage, partial coverage, and large gaps
userStories.notes: Tier: Data quality / diagnostics. Files: src/caption/models.py (CaptionResult class). Low caption coverage means the video has significant uncaptioned periods (music, silence, non-speech audio). This metric helps downstream matching understand that some video segments simply have no text to match against, rather than assuming they're low-quality matches.

userStories.title: Propagate video chapter titles to OTIO clip metadata for editor visibility
acceptanceCriteria: In otio_builder.py, when building OTIO clips, if the source segment has a chapter_title, add it to the clip's metadata dict under key 'chapter'
In xml_export.py, include chapter title as a comment or marker on clips that have chapter metadata
Clips without chapter metadata are unchanged (no empty 'chapter' key added)
Chapter metadata survives OTIO serialization and deserialization round-trip
Unit test verifies chapter metadata appears on clips and survives round-trip
userStories.notes: Tier: Output polish. Files: src/otio/otio_builder.py, src/otio/xml_export.py. When editors open the timeline in DaVinci Resolve, knowing which YouTube chapter a clip came from helps them understand the source context. This is metadata-only - no behavioral change to matching or scoring.

userStories.title: Add caption language confidence and fallback tracking
acceptanceCriteria: CaptionResult gains a 'language_confidence' field (float 0.0-1.0, default 1.0) indicating how confident the language detection is
When caption language doesn't match the requested language, language_confidence is set to 0.5 and a fallback_language field records what was used
caption_fetcher.py sets language_confidence based on whether manual captions (1.0), auto-generated in target language (0.8), or auto-generated in different language with translation (0.5) were used
Scoring can optionally apply a small penalty for low language_confidence (new config: caption_quality.language_confidence_penalty, default 0.0 - disabled by default)
Unit test verifies language_confidence values for each caption source type
userStories.notes: Tier: Quality signal. Files: src/caption/models.py (CaptionResult), src/caption_fetcher.py (language selection logic), src/matching/scoring.py. Auto-translated captions are lower quality than native language captions. Tracking this separately from the general caption_quality lets us tune penalties independently.
